column3: “The report” is rendered “the fame,” and “difficult matters” as “difficult questions.” NASB supplies “She had,” and “with her heart” is rendered “on her heart.”
“Told her all her words” is rendered “answered all her questions”; the second “told” is rendered “explain.”
Close to the Hebrew.

“The standing of his servants” is rendered “the attendance of his ministers.” “His upper room which he went up” is rendered “his stairway by which he went up”; the meaning is uncertain. “There was no more breath in her” is rendered “she was breathless.”
“Was truth the word” is rendered “It was a true report.”
“Words” is rendered “reports”; NASB supplies “it.” “You have added to the report” is rendered “You surpass the report.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“To make it stand” is rendered “establishing them”; NASB supplies “therefore.”
“Has been” is rendered “had never been.”
“Algum wood” is rendered “algum trees.”
“Tracks” is rendered “steps”; the meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain. The two stringed instruments are reversed.
NASB supplies “a return for.”
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB supplies “that which.”
NASB supplies “using” and “shekels”; “body shields” is rendered “large shields.”
NASB supplies “he made,” “using,” and “shekels.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Hands” is rendered “arms.”
“From this and from this” is rendered “on the one side and on the other”; NASB adds “other.”
“Silver was not esteemed to anything” is rendered “silver was not considered valuable.”
“One time to three years” is rendered “once every three years.” The last two animals are rendered “apes and peacocks”; the meaning of the Hebrew words is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew.
“The face of Solomon” is rendered “the presence of Solomon.”
“The matter of a year in a year” is rendered “so much year by year.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“The river” is rendered “the Euphrates River.”
“The Shephelah” is rendered “the lowland”; NASB supplies “as common” and “as plentiful.”
“Were brought out” is rendered “they were bringing.”
“Matters” is rendered “acts,” and “words” as “records.”
Close to the Hebrew.
